reformulation: Domain agent's committed reformulation (input/model.mps NAME test49 -> output/reformulated.mps NAME test49_round): 2,013 variables, 1,647 of them integer, are untouched; the 233 rows become 252 by deleting the dependent equality c50 (18 coefficients, RHS 0) and adding 20 rows round_<node> named after the 20 nodes whose balance is not a multiple of 6 (1,395 coefficients; 45-108 nonzeros each). Every added row is an exact linear combination of source rows and bound refs divided by 6: -(incident capacity rows) + sgn*balance row + 2*(flow columns with coefficient -1), i.e. C(delta(v))/6 >= ceil(|b_v|/6), then rounded by integrality of the design columns. The integer-feasible set and the objective are unchanged, the LP relaxation is strictly stronger (a complete 2,013-coordinate source point has 449/2 < 225 on round_c1). 20 added rows, 1 removed row, net 233 -> 252.

claim_class: Exact same-integer-feasible-set identity plus a one-sided LP strengthening: 3 model claims and 5 point claims. Claim 0 forward integer (source->target, projection all 2,013 coordinates, inverse present), claim 1 reverse integer, claim 2 reverse continuous (the target-LP-inside-source-LP inclusion that Strictness.inclusion_claim = 2 separates). Obligations by claim: 9,586 / 9,567 / 5,907 = 25,060, which equals the kernel's own obligations counter. Points: one complete rational source point (strictness, 52 nonzero coordinates), and integer_feasible_point plus circulation_counterexample_point each checked on the source and on the target model (52-57 nonzero entries, all others exactly zero).
claims: Claim 0, forward integer: 9,586 obligations = 2,013 VarLower + 1,647 VarUpper + 1,647 bare 'Exact' integrality checks + 252 row obligations (183 RowUpper, 49 RowEq, 20 'Local' refs for the derived round_* rows) + 1 objective 'Exact' + 2,013 projection entries + 2,013 inverse-composition residuals (tools/prepare_test49.py:16-55).

Claim 1, reverse integer: 9,567 obligations = 5,307 coordinate bounds/integrality + 233 row obligations + 1 objective + 2,013 projection + 2,013 inverse; the deleted c50 is recovered by a single Lin 'Eq' step over the 49 retained balance rows (tools/prepare_test49.py:32-35), which is block 1's only step.

Claim 2, reverse continuous (inverse None): 5,907 obligations = 2,013 VarLower + 1,647 VarUpper + 233 rows + 1 objective + 2,013 projection; this is the inclusion claim the strictness point addresses via {'Strictness':{'inclusion_claim':2}} (tools/prepare_test49.py:61-67).

Five point claims (tools/prepare_test49.py:66-71): the complete source relaxation point that satisfies all 233 original rows and 2,013 bounds but gives 449/2 < 225 on round_c1, and the tree and 2,000-unit-circulation integer points checked 'Feasible' with integers=True on both models; kernel points = 5, point_coefficient_terms = 19,278.

Edit contract: delete equality c50 with 18 coefficients; add 20 G rows with 1,395 coefficients; no variable, bound, integrality or objective coefficient changes; the kernel re-checks all 2,013 identity map entries and the 252 inverse residuals as positional obligations (attacks missing_obligation and wrong_coordinate index obligation 500 and 1500).
proof_encoding: RPA 3 text, one compact JSON object plus trailing newline: 'RPA 3\n' + json.dumps(cert,separators=(',',':')) at tools/prepare_test49.py:82; cert = {claims:[3 specs], blocks:[3 blocks], points:[5 point specs with values]}.

Block 0 (forward integer) carries the whole constructive extension: 60 steps = 40 Lin + 20 Round, i.e. per added row one Lin 'Le' with the unrounded scaled combination, one Lin 'Int' over the target row's coefficient map, one Round deriving the G row; blocks 1 and 2 have exactly one Lin step each (c50 recovery).

Every block ends in {'Return':{'map':[2,013 one-term identity expressions],'checks':[...]}}: the map arrays are literal {'constant':'0','terms':[[i,'1']]} entries of 75,385 B each (226,155 B = 32.9% of the 688,028 B RPA); checks lists total 309,222 B (44.9%).
checks are heterogeneous and positional: 13,362 bare 'Exact' (53.3%), 6,039 VarLower, 4,941 VarUpper, 549 RowUpper, 147 RowEq, 22 Local - the refs' order is the claim's obligation order.

request.json is written with indent=2 from the same claim specs (tools/prepare_test49.py:83): 308,477 B on disk versus 66,451 B compact, of which 65,811 B are the three literal 2,013-pair identity projections.
agent_manual_work: Parsed the 294,310 B MPS with fractions.Fraction and independently re-checked every body record against fixed fields ([4:12],[14:22],[24:36],[39:47],[49:61]), concluding the decimal tokens exceed traditional fixed-width numeric fields so the full tokens govern (digest section 2; eval 'Inspecting network and capacity patterns').

Recovered the model's meaning from coefficients only: 366 continuous columns each with +1/-1 in exactly two balance rows and +1 in one capacity row, 183 capacity rows each with two opposite-incidence flows and nine integer columns with coefficients 6,12,24,36,48,72,96,144,216; then built adjacency, component, bridge/articulation and duplicate-row tests (digest evals 'Verifying complete network structure' and 'Testing rounding and alternative hypotheses').

Established the 20 cut identities by hand with coefficient dictionaries: combo = sum of incident capacity rows + sgn*balance row - 2*(flow columns with coefficient -1), asserted equal to 6*target coefficients, and exhibited a BFS-tree fractional point that satisfies all 233 original rows and 2,013 bounds yet violates 12 of the 20 cuts (digest eval 'Proving strict relaxation strengthening').

Built the integer tree witness and the circulation counterexample (2,000 extra units around x5,x185,x1,x187; max flow 2,171) to falsify the tempting source-supply flow bound (digest eval 'Testing circulation-based bound hypothesis').

Hand-wrote reformulated.mps with an exact decimal formatter, re-parsed it with a second independent parser, diffed actual against intended changes (18 deleted and 1,395 added coefficients), and authored audit.json plus witnesses.json (digest section 7).
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test49.py is 119 lines with defs block, prepare, main; it imports parse_mps,row_ref from prepare_affine, expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,substitute,sha from prepare_test40, and Builder from prepare_test88 (lines 9-11) - a three-file chain of 673 further lines for primitives that are generic; plus and mul are imported but never used.

block(inp,out,claim,hints) emits the {steps, end:{Return:{map,checks}}} shape: mapping is 2,013 identity expressions; per output row it emits a RowRef for a retained row (:29-31), a Lin 'Eq' over the recovery row_multipliers for the deleted c50 (:32-35), and Lin 'Le' + Lin 'Int' + Round for each round_* row (:36-49).

Builder.lin(kind,terms,expected) recomputes the combination in Python and asserts equality with the expected expression before emitting {'Lin':{id,kind,constant,terms}} (prepare_test88.py:35-43); refexpr/kind resolve RowEq/RowUpper/VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt/Local refs (prepare_affine.py:80-88) and row_ref maps a row name to its one-key ref (prepare_affine.py:77-78).

Expression algebra is a plain dict {constant: Fraction, {var index: Fraction}} with zeros dropped, re-serialized by expr_json as {'constant':str,'terms':[[i,str]]} (prepare_test40.py:72-85); row facts come from row_fact(row,which) = -rhs - terms or its negation (prepare_test40.py:87-89).

main() runs canonical x2, assemble, verify (lines 93-97) and then five hand-mutated RPAs - continuous_integer, wrong_cut_multiplier, missing_obligation, false_strictness, wrong_coordinate - each of which must assemble and then come back INVALID, with per-attack RPA/RPX hashes recorded (lines 100-116).
friction: The derivation of each added row reaches the preparer only as an ad hoc dict: h = hints['added_rows'][name]['validity_certificate'] with keys balance_row, balance_multiplier, negated_capacity_rows, nonnegative_flow_variables_multiplier_2, unrounded_capacity_rhs, divisor (tools/prepare_test49.py:38-43); the same file carries removed_rows[...]['recovery']['row_multipliers'] (:34), and both inputs are bound to the certificate by sha256 only (cases/test49/preparation.json audit/witness_input).

The rounded RHS is hand-computed as rounded = -((-unrounded[0].numerator)//unrounded[0].denominator) and then re-asserted against the target row (:46-47), duplicating the ceiling that the domain agent's audit hints already applied; nothing in the surface exposes exact ceil of a rational.

The same 2,013-pair identity projection is written literally in every claim (tools/prepare_test49.py:64): 3 x 21,937 B = 65,811 B, which is 99.0% of the 66,451 B compact request (308,477 B as emitted with indent=2 at :83); the strictness claim is referenced only by its ordinal (inclusion_claim 2 at :66), so reordering the claim loop silently retargets it.

Each block re-materialises the full coordinate map as 2,013 literal one-term expressions {'constant':'0','terms':[[i,'1']]} - 75,385 B per block, 226,155 B = 32.9% of the RPA - although the edit touches no variable (tools/prepare_test49.py:18).

Points are emitted dense: 5 x 2,013 string values (8,086-8,188 B each, about 40.5 KB of the RPA) although each witness has only 52-57 nonzero coordinates and witnesses.json documents the sparse convention 'unlisted variables are zero' (tools/prepare_test49.py:67-71).
top_capability: TARGET_CONSTRUCTION - extending a model with derived rows and proving the extension is implied in one step: this case's entire proof content is 20 added rows, each an exact linear combination of source rows and bound refs divided by 6 and rounded by integrality, plus one deleted dependent equality. Today that is 62 hand-written steps assembled from an untyped audit dict and a hand-rolled ceiling.
notes: Scale for design purposes (no budget binds): RPA 688,028 B = 0.26% of the 256 MiB text limit, RPX 579,820 B, work 212,771 = 0.02% of 1e9, peak live facts 60, kernel execute 52 ms. The case is small and cheap (345 s agent wall, 16 turns, 0 failures - the fastest run in the corpus), so the interesting demand is not throughput but that the constructive derivation of each added row exists only as prose plus an ad hoc hint dict: 40 Lin and 20 Round steps in one claim encode 20 rows, while 53.3% of the 25,060 obligations are bare 'Exact' placeholders and 32.9% of the RPA is the identity map re-materialised per claim. Five hand-mutated certificates (continuous_integer, wrong_cut_multiplier, missing_obligation, false_strictness, wrong_coordinate) each return INVALID at exit code 2, so the attack surface around derived rows is well covered by the existing verify path; the missing piece is the constructor side.
